subject: mixed model with correlated random effects

messages.author: 0fb20183bc346dac
messages.subject: mixed model with correlated random effects
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to fit a linear mixed model with correlated random effects (intercept and slope) with R-INLA.

library("JMbayes")
library("nlme")
data(prothros)

# Example of LMM with correlated random intercept and random time slope (unstructured covariance matrix)
lmefit <- lme(pro ~ treatbin + time , random=~(1+time) |id , data=prothros)

# Equivalent fitted with INLA
y.long <- prothro$pro
linear.covariate <- data.frame(treat.l = c(data1$treatbin),time.l = c(data1$time))
random.covariate <- list(U1 = c(data1$id), V1 = c(data1$time))
joint.data <- c(linear.covariate,random.covariate)
joint.data$Y <- y.long                

LMMformula = Y ~ 1+  treat.l + time.l + f(U1, model="iid")  + f(V1, model="iid" ) 
lmminla = inla(LMM , family = c("gaussian"),
                      data = joint.data, verbose=TRUE,
                      control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,config=TRUE),
                      control.family = list( list())
                        )
summary(lmefit)
summary(lmminla )

I believe that LMMformula assumes that the random intercept and slope are not correlated.
I am wondering how I could modify it to specify that they are correlated like in lmefit.

Thanks in advance for your help,
Denise M

messages.subject: Re: mixed model with correlated random effects
parts:
Thanks very much for this suggestion Dr Rue.

I finally used "intslope" in my model formulation to assume correlated random effects in the linear mixed model fitted.
However, I still get very different coefficients from those estimated with the lme function.
Does someone have an idea of what could cause this difference?

Here is a reproducible example:

set.seed(09032020)
library("JMbayes")
library("nlme")
data(prothros)
data1 <- prothro
data1$treatbin <- as.numeric(data1$treat) -1
# Example of LMM with correlated random intercept and random time slope (unstructured covariance matrix)
lmefit <- lme(pro ~ treatbin + time , random=~(1+time) |id , data=data1 )

joint.data <- data.frame(Y=data1$pro, treatbin = c(data1$treatbin ), time = c(data1$time), subject=c(data1$id),strata=rep(1,ng),U1 = c(data1$id))
                
formula = Y ~ 1 + f(U1, model="intslope", args.intslope = list(subject = subject, covariates = time, strata=strata)) +
 treatbin + time
    
lmminla2 = inla(formula, family = c("gaussian"), data =joint.data, verbose=TRUE)
                       
summary(lmminla2)
summary(lmefit)
